title: From farm to market: the data behind Guinea-Bissau's US$30 million agrifood opportunity
gist: World Bank assessments estimate that combining agroecological farming practices with agrologistics investment (storage, roads, processing, trade facilitation) could unlock nearly $30 million a year (about 3% of agricultural GDP) in Guinea-Bissau's cashew and rice value chains, where post-harvest losses and logistics costs currently absorb 25-42% of export/retail prices.

insights.claim: Guinea-Bissau's agriculture sector contributes 30-50% of GDP and provides income for 85% of the population, and combining agroecological productivity gains with agrologistics investment could unlock nearly $30 million annually across the rice and cashew value chains alone, equivalent to about 3% of agricultural GDP.
insights.speaker: Beatriz Martinez
insights.so_what: Quantifies a specific, financeable investment case ($30M/year recurring value) for donors or agribusiness investors evaluating Guinea-Bissau's ag sector.
insights.locator: Recent World Bank assessments suggest that combining agroecological approaches

insights.claim: Guinea-Bissau is one of the world's leading raw cashew producers, with cashew accounting for more than 90% of exports and about one-quarter of national GDP, yet yields remain below 0.4 tons/hectare compared to 0.8-1 ton/hectare in India and Vietnam.
insights.speaker: Beatriz Martinez
insights.so_what: A cashew yield gap of roughly 2-2.5x versus India/Vietnam signals substantial headroom for productivity-focused agricultural investment or technology transfer in Guinea-Bissau's dominant export crop.
insights.locator: Guinea-Bissau is one of the world's leading producers of raw cashew nuts

insights.claim: Rice yields in Guinea-Bissau are around 2 tons/hectare compared to above 6 tons/hectare in most of Asia, despite rice's strategic importance to the national diet.
insights.speaker: Beatriz Martinez
insights.so_what: A 3x rice yield gap versus Asian benchmarks highlights a specific, large addressable productivity opportunity for agricultural input or intensification investment.
insights.locator: The rice sector faces similar productivity gaps

insights.claim: Guinea-Bissau lost around 188,000 hectares of tree cover between 2001 and 2021 due to land clearing for farming, contributing to soil degradation and erosion that undermines both upland and lowland farming productivity and drives further deforestation in a self-reinforcing cycle.
insights.speaker: Beatriz Martinez
insights.so_what: A concrete land-use data point for anyone assessing deforestation/ESG risk tied to agricultural expansion or commodity sourcing in Guinea-Bissau.
insights.quote: Daqui a alguns anos não poderemos mais morar aqui (In a few years we won't be able to live here anymore)
insights.locator: The country lost around 188,000 hectares of tree cover

insights.claim: Systems of Rice Intensification (SRI) and other agroecological practices have delivered results in Asia including reducing water use by 30-50% and seed requirements by 80-90%, and are proposed as transferable models for Guinea-Bissau alongside cashew-annual crop intercropping and agroforestry.
insights.speaker: Beatriz Martinez
insights.so_what: SRI's demonstrated resource-efficiency gains in Asia make it a specific, evidence-backed intervention that agricultural development financing could target in Guinea-Bissau.
insights.locator: In Asia, SRI has significantly improved yields

insights.claim: In the cashew sector, post-harvest losses can reach 25%, and agrologistics costs account for approximately 34% of the export price, with about $0.55 absorbed by transportation, handling, storage, and customs procedures for every kilogram of cashew exported.
insights.speaker: Beatriz Martinez
insights.so_what: Logistics costs consuming over a third of export value is a specific, addressable margin-recovery target for investment in storage, roads, and trade facilitation.
insights.locator: The data illustrate the scale of the challenge

insights.claim: Post-harvest losses for locally produced rice reach up to 30%, farmers receive only about one-third of the retail price, and agrologistics costs represent approximately 42% of the retail price -- about $0.48 per kilogram of rice sold -- driven by inadequate drying, storage, and milling facilities plus poor rural roads.
insights.speaker: Beatriz Martinez
insights.so_what: Farmers capturing only a third of retail value while logistics eats 42% underscores that milling/storage infrastructure investment, not just farm-level productivity, is the binding constraint on rice farmer incomes.
insights.locator: Despite the strategic importance of rice in the national diet

insights.claim: Priority investments identified include expanding secure local cashew storage, rehabilitating rural roads, digital logistics and trade facilitation tools, expanded cashew processing capacity, and expanded threshing/milling capacity for rice.
insights.speaker: Beatriz Martinez
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete, sector-specific capital-allocation roadmap for donors or agribusiness investors deciding where to deploy funds in Guinea-Bissau's ag value chains.
